name: FedSER
title: Privacy-preserving Speech Emotion Recognition through Semi-Supervised Federated Learning
tagline: Learn speech emotions from audio kept on each device
summary: Speech emotion recognition depends on sensitive audio that is costly to annotate. This work combines an attention-based speech model with federated self-training, using labeled clips and confident predictions on unlabeled clips while keeping raw audio on each device, then studies label scarcity and speaker distribution in IEMOCAP experiments.

figure.alt: An attention-based convolutional model analyzes audio spectrograms while federated clients train using labeled inputs and confidence-filtered pseudo-labels from unlabeled inputs.
figure.caption: Spectral, temporal, and channel attention help the local model represent speech. Federated self-training adds supervision from unlabeled audio, and clients share model updates with the server.

method.title: Attend to speech features
method.text: A convolutional network processes log-mel spectrograms. Spectral, temporal, and channel attention weight features before the model predicts an emotion.

method.title: Use unlabeled speech
method.text: Local self-training combines known labels with pseudo-labels from high-confidence predictions. A device-specific confidence schedule accounts for training progress and each client’s participation.

method.title: Aggregate across devices
method.text: FedAvg combines the locally trained parameters into a shared model. Raw recordings remain on devices, and the method does not require a labeled or unlabeled server dataset.

findings.title: Scarce labels still help
findings.text: On the improvised IEMOCAP subset with four emotion classes, self-training improves unweighted accuracy in all four tested partitions when only 10% of examples are labeled. The comparison uses identical labeled subsets in supervised federated baselines.

findings.title: Speaker separation is harder
findings.text: Experiments distinguish speaker-independent evaluation from overlapping speakers, and random partitioning from per-speaker non-IID data. Recognition remains harder when test speakers are unseen, underscoring the importance of the evaluation split.

abstract: Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) refers to the recognition of human emotions from natural speech. If done accurately, it can offer a number of benefits in building human-centered context-aware intelligent systems. Existing SER approaches are largely centralized, without considering users' privacy. Federated Learning (FL) is a distributed machine learning paradigm dealing with decentralization of privacy-sensitive personal data. In this paper, we present a privacy-preserving and data-efficient SER approach by utilizing the concept of FL. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first federated SER approach, which utilizes self-training learning in conjunction with federated learning to exploit both labeled and unlabeled on-device data. Our experimental evaluations on the IEMOCAP dataset shows that our federated approach can learn generalizable SER models even under low availability of data labels and highly non-i.i.d. distributions. We show that our approach with as few as 10% labeled data, on average, can improve the recognition rate by 8.67% compared to the fully-supervised federated counterparts.

provenance.figure_note: Crop from the public arXiv PDF, Figure 1, page 3; no figure labels or data modified. FedSER is a project-page shorthand; the paper is cited under its full published title. The study keeps raw audio local but does not establish a formal differential privacy guarantee.
